flashcards.title: Active Recall Flashcards
flashcards.description: Flashcards are key to mastering fact-dense UPSC questions. Click on any card below to flip it and reveal the answer.

items.question: What is the standard ratio of Harappan bricks (length:width:thickness)?
items.answer: 4:2:1. (For example: 28cm x 14cm x 7cm in standard houses).

items.question: Which site shows a radial layout of streets rather than the standard grid system?
items.answer: Banawali in Haryana, where streets radiate from the fortified citadel mound.

items.question: How did Harappans manage wastewater sanitation inside houses?
items.answer: House drains emptied into brick-lined soak pits (cesspools) beneath the street surface, filtering solid waste before water entered main drains.

items.question: Name the materials used to waterproofing the Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro.
items.answer: Gypsum mortar for binding bricks and a layer of natural bitumen (tar) to prevent leakage.

items.question: Which site utilized dressed limestone instead of baked bricks for town walls?
items.answer: Dholavira in Kutch, which also featured massive stone check dams and reservoirs.

deepDive.title: Syllabus Core Study Notes (Deep-Dive)
deepDive.description: Master the grid system, Citadel-Lower Town structures, sanitation networks, and civic engineering of the Harappan Civilisation.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
मुख्य विशेषताएं

  • ग्रिड सिस्टम (शतरंज का बोर्ड)
  • दुर्ग (उठा हुआ पश्चिमी टीला)
  • निचला शहर (आवासीय क्षेत्र)

नागरिक इंजीनियरिंग

  • मानकीकृत पकी ईंटें (1:2:4 अनुपात)
  • भूमिगत जल निकासी प्रणाली
  • रखरखाव के लिए मैनहोल कवर
  • शहरी आकारिकी
    • द्वि-विभाजित शहर: दुर्ग (शासक/धार्मिक) + निचला शहर (व्यावसायिक/आवासीय)।
    • धौलावीरा अपवाद: त्रि-विभाजित शहर (दुर्ग, मध्य शहर, निचला शहर)।
  • स्वच्छता बुनियादी ढांचा
    • जल निकासी प्रणाली ने हर घर को सड़क के नाले से जोड़ा था।
    • अपशिष्ट प्रबंधन के लिए सोख गड्ढों का उपयोग किया गया।
विशेषतामोहनजोदड़ोलोथल
लेआउटग्रिड-आयरनआयताकार/बंदरगाह शहर
किलाबंदीमजबूत दुर्गगोदीवाड़ा (कृत्रिम)

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the layout of streets in Harappan cities:
1. Main streets were aligned strictly along North-South and East-West directions to allow prevailing winds to clean them naturally.
2. Streets crossed at right angles, forming a highly organized grid iron pattern in all major settlements.
3. The street layout at Banawali deviated from the grid pattern, displaying a radial layout of roads radiating from the citadel.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, explaining the cardinal alignments, grid system, and Banawali's radial street planning.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the division of Harappan cities, consider the following statements:
1. Most settlements were divided into a western raised Citadel on a mud-brick platform and an eastern Lower Town.
2. The Citadel housed public, administrative, and religious monuments while the Lower Town was primarily residential.
3. Dholavira is uniquely divided into three fortified sections: Citadel, Middle Town, and Lower Town.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, illustrating the standard two-tier city division and Dholavira's unique three-tier planning.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Citadel-free settlements of the Indus Civilisation:
1. Chanhudaro in Sindh was a major craft suburb that completely lacked a fortified citadel mound.
2. In the absence of a citadel, Chanhudaro did not display standard Harappan weights or drainage systems.
3. Lothal had no physical wall separating its Citadel from its residential sectors.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: Chanhudaro utilized standard Harappan weights, measures, and drainage systems despite lacking a citadel. Statement 3 is incorrect: Lothal's Citadel was separated from the Lower Town by a mud-brick wall.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the drainage systems of the Indus Valley Civilisation, consider the following statements:
1. Main street drains were built of baked bricks and remained completely uncovered for air ventilation.
2. Inspection chambers or cleanup manholes were provided at regular intervals along the street drains.
3. Drains were constructed with a slight gradient or slope to ensure smooth water flow.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: Main street drains were covered with brick slabs or stone blocks to ensure public health and sanitation.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the domestic drainage inside Harappan houses:
1. Bathrooms and kitchens had brick-paved floors sloping towards a corner outlet.
2. Wastewater entered a brick-lined soak pit (cesspit) beneath the street to trap solid waste before entering public drains.
3. House drains were constructed using wooden pipes wrapped in leather at all major sites.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: House drains were constructed of baked bricks and terracotta pipes; only Kalibangan used wooden conduits, which was a regional anomaly.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the water supply in Harappan towns, consider the following statements:
1. Almost every house at Mohenjo-daro featured a private brick-lined water well.
2. Over 700 wells have been excavated at Mohenjo-daro alone.
3. Dholavira relied entirely on private household wells because surface water was absent in Kutch.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Dholavira relied on massive stone-cut reservoirs to harvest rainwater runoff because groundwater wells in Kutch were brackish and scarce.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the bricks used by Harappan builders:
1. The dimensions of both burnt and sun-dried bricks followed a strict ratio of 4:2:1 (length:width:thickness).
2. Standard brick sizes for houses were typically 28cm x 14cm x 7cm.
3. Mud-brick structures were reserved exclusively for Citadel fortifications, while private houses used burnt bricks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Mud bricks were widely used for house platforms, lower town houses, and courtyard walls, while burnt bricks were preferred where water contact was high (drains, wells, baths).

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the metrological systems of the Harappans, consider the following statements:
1. Weights were standardized cubical blocks typically carved from hard chert.
2. The binary system of weights (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64) was used for lower weights.
3. Decimal progressions were used for higher values, indicating a highly advanced mathematical scale.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct and define the standardized metrology of the Harappan trade system.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro:
1. It is a rectangular basin lined with tightly fitted baked bricks and bound with gypsum mortar.
2. Waterproofing was achieved by applying a thick layer of natural bitumen (asphalt) over the brickwork.
3. It was located in the Lower Town and was used for municipal swimming and domestic washing.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: The Great Bath was located on the Citadel and was used for collective ritual bathing and purification, not municipal washing.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the granaries in Harappan town planning, consider the following statements:
1. The Great Granary at Mohenjo-daro featured a grid of brick podiums raised to support a massive wooden superstructure.
2. Parallel rows of smaller granaries at Harappa were constructed outside the citadel near the river bank.
3. Granaries were equipped with under-floor air ventilation ducts to prevent moisture accumulation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, describing the design, location, and structural ventilation of Harappan granaries.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Dholavira's water management system:
1. It featured check dams built across seasonal streams to channel water into massive stone reservoirs.
2. The reservoirs surrounding the Citadel were cut directly into local limestone rocks.
3. Dholavira relied on a system of pottery pipelines to bring freshwater from rivers located 50 miles away.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Water was harvested locally via check dams and channels diverting seasonal runoff from Kutch's hills, not from distant rivers.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the fortifications of Harappan towns, consider the following statements:
1. Fortifications were built primarily of mud-brick, faced with burnt brick or rubble stone in peripheral areas.
2. Fortification walls featured rectangular bastions, defensive gateways, and watchtowers.
3. Sites like Chanhudaro and Balakot were enclosed by massive stone ramparts over 10 meters thick.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Chanhudaro completely lacked fortification walls, and Balakot had mud-brick defensive walls, not 10-meter stone ramparts.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the residential houses of the Harappans:
1. Houses were built facing the main avenues to facilitate commercial displays.
2. Entrance doors typically opened into side lanes rather than main streets, ensuring privacy.
3. Most houses featured a central courtyard surrounded by rooms, bathrooms, and staircases indicating double-story structures.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: Harappan house entrances opened into side alleys, and main walls facing the streets lacked windows to maintain privacy and reduce dust entry.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Kalibangan, consider the following statements:
1. The town featured separate fortifications for its Citadel and residential Lower Town.
2. The city completely lacked a public baked-brick drainage system, utilizing wooden drain pipes instead.
3. Pre-Harappan levels showed grid plowing, which aligns with the grid pattern of the mature town planning.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, describing Kalibangan's fortifications, unique wooden drains, and early agricultural grid lines.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the site of Banawali:
1. The streets did not follow a grid pattern, resulting in irregular radial layouts.
2. A fortified wall separated the Citadel from the Lower Town, yet both were built on a single mound.
3. Its drainage system was poor, using earthenware jars placed at street corners to collect waste.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct and define the regional town planning characteristics of Banawali.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the metrological standardisation, consider the following statements:
1. Weights made of chert were used primarily in Gujarat, while steatite weights were used in Punjab.
2. The standard unit of weight ratio 16 was equivalent to 13.63 grams.
3. Linear measurement systems used bronze scales and ivory rulers divided into precise units.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: Standardized chert weights were used uniformly across the entire Harappan territory, proving a centralized economic system.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Assembly Hall at Mohenjo-daro:
1. It is a large square hall containing twenty brick pillars arranged in rows.
2. It is located on the Citadel and is believed to have functioned as a municipal council hall.
3. It was decorated with relief sculptures of Harappan rulers and deities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: No relief sculptures or representations of rulers or deities have been found inside any Harappan public buildings.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to Harappan sanitary engineering, consider the following statements:
1. Wastewater from bathrooms was discharged directly onto streets to be swept away.
2. Vertical terracotta pipes embedded inside house walls channeled waste from upper floors to street drains.
3. Street drains were built below road level and paved with flat bricks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: House waste did not run onto streets; it was channeled via wall pipes into brick-lined pits or street drains to maintain cleanliness.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Dholavira's stone masonry:
1. Local dressed limestone was used for defensive gates and Citadel bastions.
2. The stone walls were coated with white gypsum plaster to prevent weathering.
3. Baked bricks were completely absent at Dholavira, even in private structures.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: While stone was the primary building material for public fortifications, baked and mud bricks were still used for private residential buildings.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Surkotada in Gujarat, consider the following statements:
1. It featured a unified fortification wall enclosing both the citadel and lower town.
2. Gateway structures constructed with stone rubble and mud-brick have been excavated.
3. The site had no drainage systems or sanitation planning.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Surkotada had standard Harappan drainage planning, with gutters and sewers, consistent with other sites in Gujarat.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the socio-political implications of Harappan planning:
1. Standardized weights, measures, and brick ratios across 1,000 miles imply central coordination.
2. The distinction between raised Citadels and Lower Towns suggests social stratification.
3. Temples and palaces are absent, indicating that civic organization did not rely on standard monarchial structures.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct and represent current scholarly interpretations of Harappan socio-political structures.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Mohenjo-daro, consider the following statements:
1. The layout is divided into a Citadel and a residential Lower Town.
2. It has yielded the famous Great Bath, pillared Assembly Hall, and Collegiate Building.
3. The site featured over 700 wells, proving highly developed groundwater management.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct and define the urban planning and monuments of Mohenjo-daro.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the site of Harappa:
1. It featured a Citadel fortified by a massive mud-brick wall faced with burnt bricks.
2. Parallel rows of circular brick threshing platforms were placed outside the Citadel near granaries.
3. Charles Masson was the first modern traveler to describe Harappa in 1826.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, describing Harappa's walls, threshing platforms, and early discovery history.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Rakhigarhi, consider the following statements:
1. It is the largest Harappan site by area, covering over nine mounds in Haryana.
2. Standardized brick planning and grid iron streets have been excavated across its mounds.
3. The site completely lacks Citadels or fortifications, showing it was a peaceful agricultural town.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Rakhigarhi has fortified mounds and citadel platforms, conforming to standard metropolitan planning.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the site of Kalibangan:
1. It is situated along the Ghaggar River channel in Rajasthan.
2. The site features a Citadel and Lower Town fortified separately.
3. Clay fire altars built on brick platforms suggest ritual fire worship.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, describing Kalibangan's geography, fortification walls, and ritual fire pits.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Dholavira, consider the following statements:
1. The city is uniquely divided into three fortified sections: Citadel, Middle Town, and Lower Town.
2. The city was surrounded by massive stone reservoirs to harvest seasonal rainwater runoff.
3. A unique 10-character gypsum signboard was found at its gateway.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, illustrating the unique urban zoning, hydraulic engineering, and script discoveries at Dholavira.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the site of Lothal:
1. It was a southern port city featuring a baked-brick tidal dockyard.
2. A mud-brick wall separated the Citadel from the Lower Town.
3. Joint double burials containing skeletons of male-female pairs were found here.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, describing Lothal's port, fortification layout, and burial findings.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Banawali, consider the following statements:
1. Streets follow a radial layout rather than a grid pattern.
2. Excavations yielded a terracotta model of an agricultural plow.
3. The drainage system was poor, using soak jars at street corners.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, describing the layout, plowing model, and drainage at Banawali.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the site of Surkotada:
1. Both the citadel and lower town are enclosed by a common stone fortification wall.
2. Skeletal remains of horses were reported in its upper layers.
3. The site is located in the Kutch district of Gujarat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, defining Surkotada's walls, horse bone findings, and geographic location.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Chanhudaro, consider the following statements:
1. It is the only major Harappan city that completely lacks a Citadel.
2. It was a craft suburb specializing in bead-making, seal-cutting, and shell-working.
3. It yielded a brick with the paw print of a dog chasing a cat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, detailing Chanhudaro's unique layout, crafts, and animal print findings.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the decline of the Harappan Civilisation:
1. R.E.M. Wheeler proposed the Aryan invasion theory based on cemetery skeletons showing trauma.
2. Modern studies link the decline to the drying up of the Ghaggar-Hakra river system due to tectonic diversions.
3. Severe, repeated floods caused by shifts in the Indus river course devastated Mohenjo-daro multiple times.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, summarizing key theories of Harappan decline.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Balakot in Balochistan, consider the following statements:
1. It was a major coastal site specializing in the shell-working industry.
2. It was fortified with mud-brick walls and watchtowers.
3. Marine shells were processed to make bangles and beads for export.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, defining Balakot's coastal geography, defenses, and shell industry.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the site of Kuntasi:
1. It functioned as a small port-cum-industrial center in Gujarat.
2. Copper metallurgy and bead manufacturing were the main economic activities.
3. The site had a small jetty for loading trade vessels.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, outlining Kuntasi's port facilities and industrial functions.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Shortughai, consider the following statements:
1. It was a mature Harappan trading enclave established in northern Afghanistan.
2. It is situated along the Amu Darya (Oxus) River.
3. It directly controlled the trade of lapis lazuli from Badakhshan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, describing Shortughai's trading function and location.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the weight system of the Harappan Civilisation:
1. Weights were standardized cubical blocks typically carved from chert.
2. The binary system was used for lower weights (up to ratio 64) and decimal for higher weights.
3. The weights were highly precise and standardized across all sites.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, describing the material, math, and standardization of weights.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to Harappan pottery, consider the following statements:
1. The pottery was predominantly wheel-made, painted in Red and Black style.
2. Common decorative motifs included geometric patterns, pipal leaves, and animal drawings like fish scales.
3. Painted pottery was highly standardized in both design and size across all sites.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, explaining the technology and standard designs of Harappan pottery.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the seals of the Indus Civilisation:
1. Seals were primarily square or rectangular blocks made of soft steatite soapstone.
2. Most seals contained short inscriptions along with animal motifs like the unicorn, zebu bull, or elephant.
3. Seals served as security tags stamped on clay sealings for commercial shipments.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, outlining the materials, designs, and functions of seals.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the terracotta figurines of the Harappan Civilisation, consider the following statements:
1. Terracotta figurines were hand-modeled and baked in kilns, representing animals, toys, and human forms.
2. The 'Mother Goddess' figurines are characterized by elaborate fan-shaped headdresses.
3. Figured toys like clay carts and whistles were common in residential sectors.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, describing terracotta human and toy figures.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding fire altars in the Harappan Civilisation:
1. Brick-lined ritual pits identified as fire altars have been found at Kalibangan and Lothal.
2. These altars often contain ash, charcoal, and clay cakes, suggesting fire worship.
3. Altars are completely absent at Mohenjo-daro and Harappa.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, outlining the fire altar findings and distributions.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to Harappan linear measurements, consider the following statements:
1. Bronze scales and ivory rulers divided into precise units have been excavated.
2. Linear standards were uniform across Punjab, Sindh, and Gujarat.
3. A standard Harappan foot was equivalent to approximately 37.6 cm.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, describing linear measurement devices and standards.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Harappan construction techniques:
1. Bricks were laid in an interlocking pattern, often called the English bond.
2. Gypsum-lime mortar was used to seal brick joins in drains and baths.
3. Pillars of stone or wood were used to support roofs in large assembly halls.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, summarizing building patterns and mortars.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Lothal's dockyard, consider the following statements:
1. The dockyard basin measured approximately 217 meters in length and 37 meters in width.
2. Sluice gates were built to trap water in the basin during low tides to float ships.
3. It was constructed using high-quality baked bricks bound with gypsum.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, describing the dimensions, gates, and bricks of the Lothal dockyard.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the site of Mohenjo-daro's Great Bath:
1. The bath is a rectangular pool measuring 12m x 7m with a depth of 2.4m.
2. North and south flights of steps led down into the water.
3. Surrounding corridors led to small rooms, one of which housed a large brick well.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, outlining the physical and architectural layout of the Great Bath.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to Harappan residential wells, consider the following statements:
1. Public and private wells were lined with wedge-shaped radial bricks to resist soil pressure.
2. Wells were placed near the outer door of houses so that travelers could use them.
3. Over 700 wells have been excavated at Mohenjo-daro.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, describing the engineering, location, and numbers of wells.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Harappan sanitary engineering:
1. Street drains were paved with flat bricks and run below the road level.
2. Houses had pottery drain conduits embedded inside the brick walls to carry waste from roofs.
3. Drains were equipped with silt traps and soak jars at junctions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, outlining sewer paving, conduits, and silt traps.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Kalibangan's wooden drainage, consider the following statements:
1. Sal or teak logs were hollowed out to form drainage conduits.
2. These wooden drains were utilized primarily in the Citadel area.
3. Kalibangan completely lacked the standard brick-lined public street sewers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, detailing the materials, locations, and unique status of Kalibangan's wooden drains.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Dholavira's check dams:
1. Stone check dams were built across the seasonal Manhar and Mansar streams.
2. Dammed water was diverted into a series of 16 interconnected reservoirs.
3. The reservoirs were cut into solid limestone and lined with stone blocks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, detailing Dholavira's damming, reservoir count, and stone masonry.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Surkotada's citadel gateway, consider the following statements:
1. The gateway featured a ramp built of rubble stone leading to the main citadel entrance.
2. Guard rooms were built flanking the gateway to monitor entry.
3. It displays a sophisticated stone arch construction representing the earliest true arch in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Harappans did not build true arches; they utilized corbelled lintels and flat stone gateways.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the site of Banawali's fortifications:
1. It featured a mud-brick wall enclosing both the Citadel and Lower Town.
2. A deep moat filled with water surrounded the outer walls of the town.
3. The Citadel was separated from the Lower Town by a fortified wall.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, outlining Banawali's wall, moat, and internal division.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Rakhigarhi's town plan, consider the following statements:
1. The settlement is divided into a Citadel and Lower Town spread over nine mounds.
2. Standardized brick platforms raisedCitadels to protect them from seasonal floods.
3. Covered brick drains with manholes are present across all mounds.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, detailing Rakhigarhi's mounds, citadels, and drains.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the metrology of the Harappan Civilisation:
1. Standardized weights were cubical blocks typically carved from chert.
2. The binary scale of weights was used for lower weights (up to ratio 64), while decimal scales were used for higher values.
3. The base unit weight ratio 16 was equivalent to 13.63 grams.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, describing the standard materials, scales, and base weights of the Harappan metrology system.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to the division of Harappan cities, consider the following statements:
1. Citadels were typically located in the west and built on mud-brick platforms, housing public monuments.
2. Lower Towns were positioned to the east, acting as larger residential areas for merchants and artisans.
3. Dholavira in Kutch is divided into three fortified sections: Citadel, Middle Town, and Lower Town.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, describing the Citadel-Lower Town dichotomy and Dholavira's three-tier layout.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Harappan sanitation and sewage system:
1. Main drains running along streets were paved with flat bricks and covered with brick slabs or stone blocks.
2. Earthenware soak jars were placed at street corners and junctions to collect solid waste before water entered public drains.
3. Drains were equipped with inspection chambers or manholes for cleaning.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, outlining the paving, soak jars, and cleanup manholes of the municipal sewage network.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Kalibangan, consider the following statements:
1. The Citadel and the Lower Town were fortified separately.
2. It lacked standard public baked-brick sewers, using hollowed-out wooden logs for drainage conduits.
3. Pre-Harappan layers yielded furrow marks showing a grid of crop plowing.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, describing the fortifications, wooden drains, and early ploughed field of Kalibangan.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the site of Banawali:
1. Streets follow a radial layout radiating from the citadel mound instead of a grid pattern.
2. Earthenware jars were placed at street corners to collect household wastewater.
3. Excavations yielded a well-preserved terracotta model of an agricultural plow.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, describing the radial plan, drainage, and plowing toy finding of Banawali.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to the Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro, consider the following statements:
1. The rectangular pool is located on the Citadel and lined with tightly fitted baked bricks.
2. Natural bitumen (asphalt) was applied over the brickwork to ensure waterproofing.
3. It was filled using a large brick-lined well located in an adjacent room.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All three statements represent verified archaeological facts about the construction, sealing, and water source of the Great Bath.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the bricks used in Harappan construction:
1. Both mud and burnt bricks followed a strict ratio of 4:2:1 (length:width:thickness).
2. Standard brick dimensions for private houses were 28cm x 14cm x 7cm.
3. Interlocking patterns, known as the English bond, were used to lay bricks for walls.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, outlining the brick ratios, house brick sizes, and interlocking English bond technique.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to Dholavira's water engineering, consider the following statements:
1. Check dams were constructed across seasonal streams like the Manhar and Mansar.
2. Dammed runoff water was diverted into a series of 16 stone-cut reservoirs.
3. Dholavira's fortifications and reservoir walls were constructed using dressed local limestone blocks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, describing the stream damming, reservoir count, and stone masonry at Dholavira.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the site of Surkotada:
1. Both the citadel and residential lower town are enclosed by a common stone fortification wall.
2. Gateway structures built of rubble stone masonry have been excavated.
3. Debated skeletal remains of horses have been reported in its upper layers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, detailing Surkotada's stone walls, stone gateway, and horse bone reports.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Chanhudaro, consider the following statements:
1. It is the only major Harappan city that completely lacks a Citadel mound.
2. It functioned as an unfortified craft suburb specializing in bead-making and shell-cutting.
3. A brick showing the paw print of a dog chasing a cat was excavated here.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All statements are correct and define the unique unfortified craft planning and animal footprint brick of Chanhudaro.

traps.title: UPSC परीक्षा के सामान्य जाल
items: जाल: यह मान लेना कि सभी हड़प्पा स्थल किलाबंद थे। वास्तविकता: चन्हुदड़ो बिना दुर्ग का एकमात्र शहर था।
जाल: सभी स्थलों पर पकी हुई ईंटों का उपयोग। वास्तविकता: कालीबंगन में निर्माण कार्य के लिए बड़े पैमाने पर कच्ची ईंटों का उपयोग किया गया।
जाल: पूर्ण एकरूपता। वास्तविकता: ग्रिड पैटर्न सार्वभौमिक है, लेकिन नगर नियोजन का पैमाना अलग-अलग स्थलों पर भिन्न है।
